title: Four of this observatory's 34 nights carry no discovery-pass trace in autonomy/log.jsonl at all -- three of them with every other nightly step present and on schedule the same night -- while memoryhole/run.py's own docstring commits this practice to writing "the empty night, which is a measurement"; discovery-pass has no equivalent floor
statement: autonomy/log.jsonl carries a step=="discovery-pass" entry for 30 of the 34 calendar nights from 2026-08-08 (this observatory's first night) through 2026-09-10 (last night); four nights carry none: 2026-08-27, 2026-08-29, 2026-08-31, 2026-09-10. For three of the four (08-29, 08-31, 09-10), every other scheduled step that runs most nights -- darkocean-run, darkocean-continuity, memoryhole-run, foreknown-notary-run (and, since 2026-09-07, registry-stall-check) -- has an entry timestamped that same calendar day, on roughly its usual schedule, proving the underlying infrastructure ran and committed that night; discovery-pass alone is absent. The fourth (08-27) is confounded with a separately documented, broader delay: foreknown-notary-run is also absent that day -- one of five nights in the whole record where it is (08-10, 08-11, 08-27, 09-04, 09-05; the other four each have their own separately documented cause and are not part of this observation) -- and the darkocean/memoryhole entries that do exist for 08-27 are timestamped 15:34-15:55 UTC rather than the usual 05:00-11:30 UTC window -- consistent with the ~11-hour scheduler delay the maintainer's own keeper PR (#38, "foreknown: the night of 2026-08-27 named as a hole, with what it cost") already named and accounted for on the foreknown-notary side. That accounting is scoped to foreknown/snapshots; it says nothing about discovery-pass, which this observation's own reviews have twice named as out of scope for the keeper's hole-accounting (obs-2026-09-06-1.json's note, restated in obs-2026-09-08-1.json's left_alone: "that step belongs to a separate scheduled keeper routine under its own delegation, not to this pass") -- correctly, since the keeper accounts for foreknown holes, not discovery-pass ones, and no keeper or discovery entry of any kind exists for 08-27, 08-29, 08-31 or 09-10 naming a discovery-pass gap specifically.
method: Read every line of autonomy/log.jsonl, grouped by the UTC calendar date of each entry's own ts field, and listed the set of distinct step values present on each of the 34 dates from 2026-08-08 through 2026-09-10 inclusive. Compared the discovery-pass date set against the full 34-night range to find the four missing dates, then re-read the full set of steps present on each missing date to check whether the surrounding infrastructure ran that night. Cross-referenced 2026-08-27 against practice/src/practice/foreknown -- no file directly documents the delay; the ~11-hour shift is read from the entry timestamps themselves (darkocean-run/darkocean-continuity/memoryhole-run at 15:xx UTC on 08-27 versus every neighbouring night's 05:00-11:30 UTC window) together with the keeper PR's own account of that night, which this observation cites for context but does not treat as committed repo evidence the way autonomy/log.jsonl and practice/src/practice/memoryhole/run.py are. Separately read practice/src/practice/staleness.py's REGISTERS tuple (the four registers sensor-registry-stall.json's promoted check watches: foreknown/snapshots, foreknown/reaction/snapshots, darkocean/snapshots, memoryhole/readings) and practice/src/practice/memoryhole/run.py's module docstring to check whether any existing, promoted mechanism already covers a silent discovery-pass night; neither does.
worth_watching_because: discovery/PROMPT.md's own header for this section reads "all optional -- an empty night is honest", and that is the right standard for what a discovery pass produces. But the record shows a stronger, unstated convention already in effect for the pass's own committed trace: on at least three nights (08-29, 08-31, 09-10) that were otherwise ordinary -- every other job ran, nothing else in the record shows an outage -- nothing about the discovery pass itself was ever written down, not even a bare log line saying it ran and found nothing. That is a different thing from an honest empty night: it is a night this capability cannot be told apart, from its own record alone, from a night it simply did not happen. sensor-registry-stall.json was promoted 2026-09-07 on exactly this reasoning applied to four other registers -- "a register silently more than a day behind, no autonomy/log.jsonl trace" is the shape every one of its four known causes shared, and the fix was a check that "never writes a register itself... so whatever silently stalled the register under watch cannot also silently stall this check" (practice/src/practice/staleness.py). Discovery-pass is not one of the four registers that check reads, and could not be added to it as written -- registry-stall compares a register's newest dated file against yesterday, and a capability whose own honest floor is silence has no dated file to compare. memoryhole/run.py already states the alternative this observatory chose for a different capability facing the identical honesty question: "write the record -- including the empty night, which is a measurement", paired in the same docstring with the caution that matters most for reading such a record afterward -- "does not call a night's silence a finding". Discovery-pass currently has neither half of that pair: no floor entry on a quiet night, and therefore no record for a future pass (or the maintainer) to read and correctly not over-interpret. This is a fact about the record, not a claim that any of the four nights failed -- three are entirely consistent with a pass that ran, found nothing to add, and (per this run's own delivery instructions) correctly did not commit anything at all; the record as it stands cannot distinguish that from the routine having simply not fired. That ambiguity, not any specific missing night, is the difference worth watching.
left_alone: Not proposing a sensor or a code change for this tonight. A mechanical check would need either a dated file discovery-pass writes on every night regardless of outcome (which would mean changing the "do not commit an empty night" convention itself, one layer up from anything this pass's own delegation covers -- that convention is not written in discovery/PROMPT.md, it comes from this run's own outer delivery instructions, and changing how a future run is told to deliver is not a decision this file can make for it) or a purely external check (comparing GitHub's own PR history against calendar dates) that would depend on evidence outside the committed repo, which no proposal file in foreknown/proposals/ has ever cited and which this observation deliberately did not lean on for its core claim. Naming the gap and its evidence is what tonight's delegation covers; deciding whether discovery-pass should adopt memoryhole's "write the empty night" convention is the maintainer's to make. Not investigating why the three clean nights (08-29, 08-31, 09-10) were silent -- infrastructure outside this working tree, out of the delegation charter (public, no login, no cost, no personal data) and not evidenced by any committed file either way. Not re-opening sensor-registry-stall.json's own review chain -- its four watched registers and their promoted threshold are unaffected; this observation names a fifth thing worth the same shape of attention, not a defect in the four already covered. Checked and left alone: sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json (gdacs-tc-1001305 still OPEN, last REVISED 2026-09-03, no second closure); sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json (gdacs-fl-1103815's datemodified still frozen at 2026-09-03T13:36:40 across all five nights checked since the 2026-09-08 review, 09-06 through 09-10 -- the freeze continues to hold, no new instance to add); the two maintainer-deferred, deliberately-unmerged export PRs (#46, #49) touching darkocean's published figures -- both explicitly wait on the maintainer's own choice of methodology, not on anything this pass can settle. No memoryhole verdicts: memoryhole/readings/2026-09-09.json, the newest reading, carries zero rule-layer abstentions across 71 entries.
